harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: On node1, /srv/data is now a dedicated XFS filesystem (loop-mounted from /var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img, persisted in /etc/fstab with the uquota mount option) enforcing a 100MB hard/soft filesystem-level user quota for datauser via XFS's native quota subsystem. Since the node's root filesystem is XFS mounted noquota and quota options cannot be changed via live remount on a running root fs, a separate quota-enabled XFS image was created and mounted at /srv/data instead of touching root fs boot parameters. Enforcement was verified both before and after a full node restart: writes past 100MB fail with "Disk quota exceeded", and the quota-enabled mount and limit configuration survive reboot via fstab.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 10, root fs is XFS on /dev/vda4 mounted noquota; /srv/data and datauser did not yet exist
Confirmed xfs_quota/xfsprogs available
Created a 2G sparse XFS image at /var/lib/srv-data-backing/srv-data.img and loop-mounted it at /srv/data with the uquota option
Created datauser, chowned /srv/data to datauser, and set a 100M soft/hard XFS user quota via 'xfs_quota -x -c limit'
Added a persistent /etc/fstab entry for the loop-mounted quota filesystem
Verified enforcement: a datauser write of 150M failed at exactly 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded'
Cleaned up test file and confirmed fstab persistence by unmounting and remounting via mount -a
Captured pre-restart baseline evidence (boot_id, mount state, quota report, account)
Issued a deferred systemctl reboot on node1 so the acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 until it became reachable again and confirmed the boot_id changed, proving a genuine restart
Re-verified post-restart: quota mount active, quota limits intact, and a 150M write by datauser again failed at 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded'
Removed the post-restart test file, leaving /srv/data empty with quota usage at 0

evidence.requirement: datauser limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: xfs_quota set 100M soft/hard limit for datauser on /srv/data; dd write of 150M by datauser failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' after exactly 100M written

evidence.requirement: quota is enforced by the filesystem itself (not application-level)
evidence.summary: /srv/data mounted as XFS with uquota kernel-level quota accounting; kernel itself rejected the write beyond the block limit
Added fstab entry for the loop-mounted quota filesystem; unmount+mount -a reloaded it with usrquota active and limits intact
Captured boot_id, mount state showing usrquota active, and quota report showing datauser 100M soft/hard before restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: Deferred systemctl reboot backgrounded with a 2s delay; exec call returned 'reboot-scheduled' successfully before the node went down

evidence.requirement: proof node1 actually restarted (changed boot identity)
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 368725cb-c64e-4393-b25f-da5111703b4a (pre-restart) to 7a9fb09f-23cb-4fb5-9a43-90ece988e545 (post-restart, uptime 0 min), with connection failures in between confirming the node was actually down

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of quota enforcement and data
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/data remounted automatically with usrquota via fstab, quota report showed datauser's 100M limit intact, and a fresh 150M write by datauser again failed at exactly 100M with 'Disk quota exceeded'
